# UK VAT Rules (2026/27)

## Registration Thresholds

- **Mandatory registration**: VAT-taxable turnover exceeds **£90,000** in any rolling 12-month period (raised from £85,000 on 1 April 2024) — OR you expect to exceed £90,000 in the next 30 days alone
- **Voluntary registration**: any business can register voluntarily (useful for reclaiming input VAT)
- **Deregistration threshold**: **£88,000** — can deregister if taxable turnover falls below this
- **Distance selling**: different rules for selling to EU consumers (OSS scheme)
- Source: <https://www.gov.uk/vat-registration/when-to-register>

## VAT Rates

| Rate | Percentage | Applies to |
|------|-----------|------------|
| Standard | 20% | Most goods and services |
| Reduced | 5% | Domestic energy, children's car seats, smoking cessation products |
| Zero-rated | 0% | Most food, books, newspapers, children's clothing, public transport |
| Exempt | N/A | Insurance, finance, education, health, land (in some cases) |

### Key distinctions
- **Zero-rated vs exempt**: zero-rated businesses can still reclaim input VAT; exempt businesses cannot
- **Mixed supplies**: if you sell both taxable and exempt, you're "partially exempt" — complex input VAT rules apply

## VAT Schemes

### Standard Accounting
- Account for VAT when you invoice (not when you get paid)
- Reclaim VAT on purchases when you receive the invoice
- Suitable for most businesses

### Cash Accounting Scheme
- Account for VAT when you receive payment (not when you invoice)
- Reclaim VAT when you pay suppliers
- **Available if VAT-taxable turnover ≤ £1,350,000**. Must leave when turnover exceeds **£1,600,000**
- Good for businesses with long payment terms
- Source: <https://www.gov.uk/vat-cash-accounting-scheme>

### Flat Rate Scheme
- Pay a fixed percentage of gross turnover (incl VAT) to HMRC
- Cannot reclaim input VAT (except on capital goods over £2,000)
- **Available if VAT-taxable turnover (excl VAT) ≤ £150,000**. Must leave when total business income (incl VAT) exceeds **£230,000**
- Percentage varies by sector (e.g., 14.5% for computer services, 11% for accountancy, 16.5% for limited cost traders)
- 1% discount in first year of VAT registration
- Source: <https://www.gov.uk/vat-flat-rate-scheme>

### Annual Accounting Scheme
- Submit one VAT return per year instead of quarterly
- Make 9 interim payments through the year
- **Available if VAT-taxable turnover ≤ £1,350,000**. Must leave when turnover exceeds **£1,600,000**
- Final balancing payment with the annual return
- Source: <https://www.gov.uk/vat-annual-accounting-scheme>

## VAT Returns

### Standard quarterly returns
- VAT periods are typically aligned to calendar quarters, but can be set to any 3-month cycle
- Return due: **1 calendar month and 7 days** after the end of the VAT period
- Payment due by the same date
- Must include the 9-box calculation
- Source: <https://www.gov.uk/vat-returns/deadlines>

### The 9 Boxes
1. VAT due on sales (output tax)
2. VAT due on acquisitions from EU
3. Total VAT due (Box 1 + Box 2)
4. VAT reclaimed on purchases (input tax)
5. Net VAT (Box 3 - Box 4) — pay this or reclaim
6. Total sales excluding VAT
7. Total purchases excluding VAT
8. Total EU supplies excluding VAT
9. Total EU acquisitions excluding VAT

## Making Tax Digital (MTD)

### MTD for VAT — mandatory now
- All VAT-registered businesses must use MTD-compatible software
- Mandatory since April 2022 for all VAT-registered businesses regardless of turnover
- Must keep digital records, with digital links between software (no manual re-keying)

### MTD for Income Tax (ITSA) — phased rollout
- **From 6 April 2026** (current tax year): mandatory for sole traders and landlords with gross income over **£50,000**. Quarterly digital submissions plus one Final Declaration.
- **From 6 April 2027**: extends to those with gross income over **£30,000**
- **Expected from 6 April 2028**: extends to those with gross income over **£20,000** (subject to legislation)
- Quarterly submission deadlines: Q1 due 7 Aug, Q2 due 7 Nov, Q3 due 7 Feb, Q4 due 7 May. Final Declaration due 31 January after tax year end.
- Source: <https://www.gov.uk/guidance/check-if-youll-need-to-sign-up-for-making-tax-digital-for-income-tax>

## Late Filing Penalties

### Points-based system (from January 2023)
- 1 point per late submission
- Penalty threshold depends on submission frequency:
  - Annual: 2 points
  - Quarterly: 4 points
  - Monthly: 5 points
- Once threshold reached: **£200 penalty per late return**
- Points expire after 24 months of compliance

### Late payment penalties
- Up to 15 days late: no penalty (interest still accrues)
- 16-30 days late: 2% of outstanding VAT
- 31+ days late: 2% + further 2% of remaining balance
- Daily interest at Bank of England base rate + 2.5%

## Common VAT Mistakes

1. Not registering on time when turnover crosses £90,000 (rolling 12-month basis, not financial year)
2. Claiming input VAT on client entertaining (never allowed)
3. Wrong VAT rate on mixed supplies
4. Not adjusting for private use of business assets
5. Forgetting to account for reverse charge on services from abroad
6. Picking the wrong flat rate sector percentage
